instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a rice cooker or a covered pot.
Cut each of the 4 tomatoes into 8 wedges. Roughly chop the 4 garlic cloves. Thinly slice 2 of the green onions and roughly chop a small handful of the cilantro.
Crack the 6 eggs into a bowl. Add the 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and beat them lightly with a fork, only until the yolks and whites are mixed.

When the rice is nearly done, heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the garlic and stir it for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant and is only starting to turn golden.
Add the tomatoes and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until the skins blister and loosen and the juice runs into the pan.
Sprinkle in 2 tsp brown sugar and 1/4 tsp of the salt and stir them through.
Turn the heat down to medium and pour the eggs over the tomatoes. Leave them for about 20 seconds, until the edges start to set.
Push the set egg toward the middle with a spatula and tip the pan so the runny egg flows into the gaps. Keep folding gently for 1 to 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look a little wet. They keep cooking in the hot pan.
Taste it. If it's flat, add some of the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Scatter the green onions and cilantro over the top.
method_notes: All three keep it to ripe tomatoes, eggs, a little sugar and salt, cooked fast in one pan and served over rice. Nomss, the lead, softens garlic in oil, blisters tomato wedges with brown sugar and salt, then pours the eggs, seasoned with chicken bouillon powder and Shaoxing wine, straight over the tomatoes and folds them in. The Posh Journal scrambles the eggs first, cooks the tomatoes with green onion, soy sauce and sugar and folds the eggs back in, and No Recipes stirs ketchup and starch into the tomatoes before the eggs go over. This one follows Nomss, sized up to 6 eggs and 4 tomatoes for four.
